# Rudis — Funding Strategy & Target Ladder (2026)

**Purpose:** avoid dependence on a single investor or strategic partner while preserving founder autonomy and financing optionality.

`ONE FUNDER != ONE FUTURE`

`CAPITAL DIVERSIFICATION -> NEGOTIATING POWER`

## 1. Tier A — Strategic partner financing

Primary target: Meta or another large AI / agent / immersive-platform company.

Preferred instrument:

- staged strategic R&D agreement;
- up to USD 12M initial program;
- optional later program only by separate approval;
- no automatic exclusivity;
- no automatic Canon / governance rights;
- Founder Strategic Reserve >=10% target;
- explicit founder compensation / liquidity mechanism negotiated separately.

Purpose:

- technical validation;
- reference integration;
- partner access;
- market signal;
- non-dilutive or limited-dilution capital where possible.

## 2. Tier B — Spanish public / quasi-public company financing

### ENISA

Publicly available ENISA financing currently includes participative loans from approximately EUR 25,000 to EUR 1.5M for Spanish innovative SMEs, without ENISA taking company ownership or management participation and generally without traditional guarantees.

Strategic value for Rudis:

- comparatively founder-friendly control profile;
- compatible with preserving management autonomy;
- useful as co-financing / runway alongside strategic money;
- requires an eligible Spanish company and financial conditions including adequate own funds.

Use case:

- operating company establishment;
- engineering and commercialization runway;
- leverage alongside equity / founder capital / strategic financing.

### CDTI — continuous innovation financing

CDTI maintains continuous company financing instruments for applied innovation, including partially repayable support for eligible company projects.

Strategic value:

- can fund technical development without transferring constitutional or investor governance rights;
- may support a defined RAL / StateOS commercial R&D package;
- requires an eligible company, project budget and formal financial capacity.

Use case:

- reproducibility / integration / commercialization engineering;
- partner-specific technical development;
- infrastructure and applied innovation.

NEOTEC 2026 is already in its 2026 procedure and is not treated here as an immediate new application route; future editions should be monitored.

## 3. Tier C — European deep-tech funding

### EIC Accelerator 2026

EIC Accelerator Open is available for innovations in any technology field. The 2026 program includes grant and investment possibilities; the next published 2026 batching date after early September is 4 November 2026.

Potential Rudis framing:

> Verifiable authority infrastructure for action-capable AI: a model-agnostic execution and evidence layer separating agent capability from legitimate authority.

Before application Rudis should have:

- a suitable SME / startup legal vehicle;
- defensible IP / freedom-to-operate position;
- clear commercialization path;
- measurable market problem;
- technical proof beyond architecture alone;
- credible team / delivery plan.

### Horizon Europe / Digital

Current EU digital R&I priorities include trustworthy AI, data, strategic technological autonomy and virtual worlds.

Rudis may fit better as a consortium technology / research work package than as an isolated constitutional project.

Preferred framing:

- trustworthy agent execution;
- verifiable authorization and causal receipts;
- European digital sovereignty;
- agent safety / interoperability;
- virtual-world governance infrastructure.

## 4. Tier D — Private venture / strategic capital

Only after minimum financing readiness:

- legal vehicle;
- IP map;
- clean public surface;
- one exact technical candidate;
- one strong demo;
- initial partner / user validation;
- founder-autonomy term principles.

Preferred investors:

- deep-tech funds;
- AI infrastructure funds;
- cyber/security investors;
- open-source commercial-model investors;
- strategic corporate venture arms.

Avoid optimizing for the highest nominal valuation if the terms materially constrain founder freedom or transfer broad IP rights.

## 5. Capital stack — preferred order

A strong path could be:

```text
FOUNDER / EARLY CAPITAL
+ PUBLIC / QUASI-PUBLIC FINANCING
+ STRATEGIC R&D PARTNER
+ SELECTIVE EQUITY
= DIVERSIFIED CAPITAL STACK
```

This reduces dependence on any one party.

## 6. Freedom-preserving principle

Where funding is project-restricted, founder personal autonomy should be created transparently through:

- founder compensation;
- lawful liquidity / transaction consideration;
- Founder Strategic Reserve at project level;
- retained background IP and retained fields;
- limited exclusivity;
- no broad personal guarantees;
- no blanket future-IP assignment.

## 7. Immediate sequence

1. establish / select contracting vehicle;
2. obtain Spanish legal + tax review;
3. finish IP / contributor inventory;
4. produce Meta / strategic deck and demo;
5. begin strategic outreach;
6. prepare ENISA eligibility package once company capital structure is known;
7. assess CDTI project fit;
8. prepare EIC Accelerator short proposal if SME / maturity criteria are satisfied;
9. raise private equity only from a position where alternatives already exist.

## 8. Negotiation objective

> Rudis should reach the table with more than one path to capital. A founder with only one possible source of money negotiates price. A founder with several credible sources negotiates structure, freedom and long-term alignment.
